subject: GridPay SLA redlines and runbook coordination
messages:
From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@gridpay.com>
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Michael Tran <michael.tran@gridpay.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Order Form redlines — SLA uptime & credits

Rafael — thanks again for the call this morning. Attaching GridPay's initial redline of the order form focused on SLA and maintenance language. High-level asks:

- Move uptime target from 99.9% to 99.99% for production (customer-facing) traffic.
- Remove/raise the credit cap on cumulative monthly credits (we're pushing for uncapped credits beyond a threshold).
- Shorten P1 response time from 1 hour to 30 minutes and require a 2-hour mitigation/update cadence until resolution.
- Limit scheduled maintenance to a single weekly 2-hour window per region and require 72-hour advance notice; exclude emergency maintenance only with explicit consent.

Also attaching a short excerpt of our runbook so you can validate rollback/runbook language in the order form. We'll need clear handoff points for incidents that may affect settlement windows.

Attachments: [gridpay_redlines_v1.pdf (pdf)], [gridpay_runbook_excerpt.txt (text)]

Can your legal and ops teams review and give a proposed response by end of day Thursday? If you prefer, we can do a 20-minute call to walk through tradeoffs.

Thanks,
Emily Zhao
Head of Platform Reliability | GridPay
emily.zhao@gridpay.com
+1 (415) 555-0189

From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@gridpay.com>
Cc: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 10 Jun 2025 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — SLA uptime & credits

Emily — appreciate the clear asks and the runbook excerpt. Looping in Lauren (legal), Rachel (ops), and Aditya (SRE/measurements) to coordinate. Quick points from my side:

- Uptime target: 99.99% is a material change with significant capacity and cost implications. We typically offer a 99.9% production SLA with a tiered credit schedule. We can propose a narrower maintenance exclusion window and a higher credit tier at 99.95% for customers committing to reserved capacity.

- Credits cap: we can increase the monthly cap and add an escrow-style carveout for sustained outages, but uncapped credits are very challenging without an alternative commercial commitment.

- Response times: happy to tighten the P1 response to a 45-minute initial response and 90-minute update cadence as a compromise. For 30-minute initial response we need a dedicated on-call resource in your time-zone and a higher commitment.

- Scheduled maintenance: we can agree to a single weekly 2-hour window per region with 72-hour notice for planned work. Emergency maintenance still needs to be permitted for safety/security fixes, but we can add an "emergency approval" path that notifies designated GridPay contacts and offers rollback guarantees.

Action items: Lauren — can you propose specific redline language for the credit cap and emergency maintenance carveouts?
Rachel — can you review the runbook excerpt and flag any operational showstoppers (rollback SLAs, rollback playbook timing)?
Aditya — can you confirm how availability will be measured (per-tenant 5xx rate vs. aggregated)?

If helpful, I can consolidate a short amendment (1–2 pages) that frames the commercial options for GridPay (hosted vs reserved capacity) so we can align commercial levers with SLA commitments. Happy to set a 20-minute call tomorrow.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: proposed_sla_amendment_draft.docx]

From: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
To: rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com, Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@gridpay.com>
Cc: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Wed, 11 Jun 2025 09:12:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Order Form redlines — SLA uptime & credits (legal redlines attached)

Thanks, Rafael and Emily. I've reviewed GridPay's redlines and drafted legal track changes with alternative language that balances GridPay's ask and Redwood's operational constraints. Summary of proposed legal positions: 

1) Uptime measurement and metric: define "Availability" as inbound request success rate measured at the per-tenant load-balancer egress with a 5xx/timeout threshold; specify 30-day rolling measurement window. This avoids noisy minute-by-minute fluctuations.

2) Credit structure: introduce a two-tier credit model: a higher uncapped multiplier for incidents meeting the "Sustained Partial Outage" definition (>= 6 hours continuous impact affecting >= 20% requests), and a capped monthly credit for isolated incidents. This gives GridPay protection for prolonged events while limiting exposure for brief spikes.

3) Maintenance windows: accept the single weekly 2-hour window with 72-hour notice for planned maintenance. For emergency maintenance, add an explicit "emergency operations" definition and require Redwood to notify GridPay POCs as soon as practicable; include a rollback requirement where feasible.

4) Response time wording: propose an "initial response" metric (acknowledgement and triage) within 45 minutes for P1s and a subsequent update every 2 hours until mitigation plan is in place. If GridPay purchases a priority support add-on (reserved capacity), we can offer 30-minute initial response.

I've attached the tracked redlines document (redlines_legal_track.docx) with precise language for insertion into the order form and MSA. Please review and let me know if GridPay is comfortable with the two-tier credit approach — it's our primary compromise to address the uncapped credit request.

Next steps: Rafael to confirm commercial options (reserved capacity / priority support) and provide a brief amendment; Emily to confirm which POCs we should notify for emergency maintenance. If GridPay wants to accept the legal track I'll prepare a DocuSign packet.

Regards,
Lauren Bishop
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com
[Attachment: redlines_legal_track.docx]

From: Emily Zhao <emily.zhao@gridpay.com>
To: lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com, rafael.mendes@redwoodinference.com
Cc: rachel.kim@redwoodinference.com, aditya.rao@redwoodinference.com
Date: Thu, 12 Jun 2025 16:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Order Form redlines — SLA uptime & credits

Lauren / Rafael — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clearer legal language. The two-tier credit structure is promising; GridPay can live with a "Sustained Partial Outage" clause if the thresholds are explicit and the measurement window is per-tenant. A couple of clarifying asks before we sign: 

- Emergency maintenance: please add an explicit escalation path and a weekend-oncall notification requirement for emergencies that could cause customer impact. We need a contact and a phone escalation in addition to email.
- Rollback guarantees: we would like a back-out plan to be documented in the runbook and a commitment to attempt rollback when a change increases errors by >5% within the first 15 minutes after rollout.
- Credits timing: can credits be applied in the billing cycle immediately following detection and agreed root cause? We want faster remediation to our invoices.

I'll attach a 1-page runbook excerpt with our preferred notification fields and contacts. We can take a 20-minute call tomorrow at 11:00 PT to finalize a short amendment and DocuSign if that works for you. If you confirm, we'll prepare the internal procurement approval to expedite.

Attachments: [gridpay_runbook_excerpt.txt (text)]

Thanks,
Emily
